# CAL-G01 Runtime Payload Capture

**Document type:** Runtime evidence capture (not design, not implementation)
**Mode:** Capture only — **no mapping, no adapter, no `createCase()`, no Notion write, no Case/Offer/Workflow/Dashboard/Customer/OCR touched**
**Date:** 2026-08-05
**Source:** exactly one real, production `BOOKING_CREATED` webhook delivery, generated by an actual booking on `https://cal.com/watermotion/60min` and received by the live production endpoint `https://serviceportal.onrender.com/api/cal/webhook`
**Capture mechanism:** temporary, observational-only logging added in commit `a8b1cdc4` (`api/cal-routes.js`), deployed to production, gated strictly to `triggerEvent === 'BOOKING_CREATED'`. No business logic, Case creation, or Notion write was touched by this capture.
**Evidence chain:** Cal.com dashboard (webhook config, ping test) → real booking via `https://cal.com/watermotion/60min` → Render production log line `[cal_g01_capture]` (timestamp `2026-08-05T08:40:04.356Z`, correlationId `cal-75847a40609f`)

**Redaction applied to this document only** (the transient production log line itself, and the live Cal.com booking record, still hold the unredacted values — this document is the shareable artifact): customer name, email, phone, home address, and LINE ID are replaced with `[REDACTED-*]` markers. All keys, structure, types, and non-personal values are preserved exactly as received — nothing renamed, nothing normalized, nothing guessed.

---

## Observed event type

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `triggerEvent` (top-level) | `"BOOKING_CREATED"` |
| `payload.type` (slug) | `"60min"` |
| `payload.eventTypeId` | `6040165` |
| `payload.eventTypeTitle` | `"Free Water Check"` |

Three independent ways to identify the event type exist in the payload: numeric `eventTypeId`, slug `type`, and human title `eventTypeTitle`. This directly resolves the "event type identifier" unknown from every prior CAL-G01 template — future CAL-G03 attribution mapping should key off `eventTypeId` (stable, numeric) rather than the human-editable title.

## Observed booking id

| Field | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `payload.uid` | `"tnLhVTCWh2CzFWcnZgdCbC"` | The value used elsewhere in Cal.com's own UI/URLs for this booking (matches the booking confirmation page URL) |
| `payload.iCalUID` | `"tnLhVTCWh2CzFWcnZgdCbC@Cal.com"` | Same identifier, iCal-formatted |
| `payload.bookingId` | `23398229` | A **separate**, numeric, internal Cal.com booking id — not the same value or format as `uid` |

**Three identifiers exist, not one.** This was not anticipated in any prior document. `uid` is the natural candidate for `calBookingId` (matches Cal.com's own public-facing booking reference), but this capture is a single `BOOKING_CREATED` event only — **whether `uid` (or `bookingId`) survives a reschedule is still not proven by this evidence** and remains open exactly as flagged in every prior gate document. This capture does not close that specific question; only a captured `BOOKING_RESCHEDULED` payload for the same booking can.

## Observed attendee fields

| Field | Path | Present |
|---|---|---|
| Name | `payload.attendees[0].name`, also split into `.firstName`/`.lastName` | ✅ (redacted here) |
| Email | `payload.attendees[0].email` | ✅ (redacted here) |
| Phone | `payload.attendees[0].phoneNumber` | ✅ (redacted here) — E.164 format (`+66...`); **note:** the raw form input was rejected until formatted as `+66XXXXXXXXX` — a bare local-format number (`08XXXXXXXX`) failed Cal.com's own client-side validation, so E.164 appears to be enforced at the source, not just a formatting preference |
| Attendee timezone | `payload.attendees[0].timeZone` | ✅ — `"Asia/Bangkok"` |
| LINE ID | `payload.responses["Line-ID"].value` and duplicated at `payload.userFieldsResponses["Line-ID"].value` | ✅ (redacted here) — custom question, **not** a fixed Cal.com field |
| Home address | `payload.responses.location.value.optionValue` | ✅ (redacted here) — **structural finding:** this is not a flat string; it's a nested object `{ value: "somewhereElse", optionValue: "<the actual address text>" }` |
| "What is this meeting about?" | `payload.responses.title.value` | Present, `isHidden: true` in this booking's response set |
| "Property Type" | `payload.responses["Property-Type"]` | **Configured but not active** — object present with only `{ label, isHidden: true }`, no `.value` key at all |
| "Main concern" | `payload.responses["Main-concern"]` | Same as Property Type — configured, `isHidden: true`, no value |
| "How did you hear about us?" | `payload.responses["How-did-you-hear-about-us"].value` | ✅ — `"Other"` (test-selected; not PII) |
| "Location" (URL field, distinct from "Home address") | `payload.responses.Location.value` | ✅ — free-text URL supplied during the test booking; not customer PII, left as-is |
| Additional notes | `payload.responses.notes.value`, duplicated at top-level `payload.additionalNotes` | ✅ (redacted here per explicit instruction) |

**New finding not anticipated in any prior document:** `Property-Type` and `Main-concern` exist as configured custom questions on this event type (their labels are present) but were **not rendered/required** in this booking's actual flow (`isHidden: true`, no `.value`). This means CAL-G01's field checklist should mark these two as "configured, conditionally inactive" rather than assuming they're always required — the earlier assumption that all listed form fields are always present was not correct for these two.

## Observed metadata

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `payload.startTime` | `"2026-08-31T07:00:00.000Z"` (ISO 8601, UTC, `Z` suffix) |
| `payload.endTime` | `"2026-08-31T08:00:00.000Z"` |
| `payload.organizer.timeZone` | `"Asia/Bangkok"` |
| `payload.organizer.utcOffset` | `420` (minutes = UTC+7) — **explicit numeric offset is provided**, not just a timezone name |
| `payload.attendees[0].utcOffset` | `420` |
| `payload.length` | `60` (minutes) |
| `payload.status` | `"ACCEPTED"` |
| `payload.requiresConfirmation` | `false` |
| `payload.price` / `payload.currency` | `0` / `"usd"` |
| `payload.destinationCalendar[0].integration` | `"google_calendar"` |
| `payload.organizer.email` | `hi@water-motion.co` — **not redacted**: this is the business's own account/organizer contact, already publicly listed in the site footer, not customer PII |
| HTTP `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| HTTP `X-Cal-Signature-256` | present, literal value `"no-secret-provided"` (confirms: Cal.com always sends this header, and substitutes this exact placeholder string when no webhook secret is configured on the Cal.com side — it does not omit the header) |
| Body length | `4396` bytes |

**Timezone question resolved:** every prior document marked "timezone representation" as `UNKNOWN`. This capture proves Cal.com sends UTC `Z`-suffixed ISO timestamps for `startTime`/`endTime`, plus separate explicit `timeZone` (IANA name) and `utcOffset` (minutes) fields on both `organizer` and each attendee. No ambiguity remains for this event type.

### Missing fields (anticipated in prior CAL-G01 templates, not found in this capture)

- **A distinct webhook delivery/event id** — no field in the JSON body corresponds to "delivery id" as a separate concept from the booking `uid`. If Cal.com provides one, it was not observed in the body; it may live in an HTTP header this capture did not log (see Known gaps below).
- **`campaignOffer`/campaign field** — does not exist as a native Cal.com field, confirming the DDR's original assumption that campaign attribution must be *derived* from `eventTypeId`, never read directly off the payload.

### Unknown/unanticipated fields (present in this capture, not predicted by any prior document)

- `payload.bookingId` (separate numeric id alongside `uid`)
- `payload.responses` vs `payload.userFieldsResponses` — two overlapping-but-not-identical objects (the latter is a subset containing only custom questions)
- The nested `{ value, optionValue }` shape for the "Home address" response specifically (not a flat string, unlike every other text response)
- `payload.appsStatus` / `payload.destinationCalendar` — Google Calendar integration metadata, irrelevant to Case mapping but present
- `payload.disableRescheduling` / `disableCancelling` and their `*Scope` fields — booking-level policy flags not previously discussed
- `payload.assignmentReason`, `payload.metadata` — present but empty in this capture; unknown whether they populate under other conditions (e.g., round-robin assignment, which this single-host event type doesn't use)

### Known gaps in this capture (honest limitations, not filled in)

1. **Full HTTP headers were not logged** — the capture code logged only `Content-Type` and the `X-Cal-Signature-256` value, not the complete header set. If a delivery/idempotency id exists as a header (not in the body), it was not captured this round.
2. **Only `BOOKING_CREATED` was captured.** `BOOKING_CANCELLED` and `BOOKING_RESCHEDULED` payloads — and specifically whether `uid`/`bookingId` survive a reschedule — remain uncaptured and unproven.
3. **`Property-Type` and `Main-concern` being `isHidden: true`** was observed for this specific booking flow; it is not yet known whether a different path through the booking form would activate them.

## CAL-G01 declaration

## **CAL-G01 READY** (for the `BOOKING_CREATED` event specifically — `BOOKING_CANCELLED`/`BOOKING_RESCHEDULED` remain uncaptured)

**Rationale:** every field this document's field inventory needed — booking identifier(s), attendee identity fields, appointment start/end with unambiguous timezone representation, event type identification, and the full custom-question response shape — is now backed by real, observed runtime evidence, not documentation or guesswork. The JSON tree, field inventory, and payload above are ready to freeze a `BOOKING_CREATED` mapper contract against.

**Not covered by this declaration:**
- `BOOKING_CANCELLED` and `BOOKING_RESCHEDULED` payload shapes are still unproven — a mapper/adapter for those events would still be guessing.
- Whether `uid` survives a reschedule is still unproven (requires a captured reschedule event on this same booking).
- Full HTTP headers beyond Content-Type and the signature header were not captured this round.

---

## Stop condition

Per instruction: **capture complete, stopping here.** No mapping, no adapter, no `createCase()` call, and no Notion write were implemented or invoked at any point in this exercise. Awaiting architecture approval before any Phase 3+ work begins.
